1	# cybernaut-mini
2	
3	An educational, local-first replica of the retrieval architecture described in
4	the NOSIBLE Cybernaut posts:
5	
6	- [The Road to Cybernaut-1](https://nosible.com/blog/the-road-to-cybernaut-1)
7	- [Introducing Cybernaut-1: Agentic Search with MCTS](https://nosible.com/blog/introducing-cybernaut-1-agentic-search-with-mcts)
8	
9	**This project is unaffiliated with NOSIBLE and makes no claim of benchmark
10	parity. It is a clean-room, educational implementation written for learning
11	purposes only.**
12	
13	---
14	
15	## Architecture
16	
17	```mermaid
18	graph LR
19	    A[documents.jsonl] -->|ingest| B[Shard & Embed]
20	    B -->|MiniBatchKMeans| C[Index Artifacts]
21	    C -->|LoadedIndex| D[Router]
22	    D -->|top-N shards| E[Retrieve]
23	    E -->|lexical + dense + RRF| F[Stage 1: Explore]
24	    F -->|UCT select| G[Stage 2: Refine]
25	    G -->|UCT select| H[Stage 3: Exploit]
26	    H -->|winner replay| I[SearchHit list + AgentTrace]
27	```
28	
29	The build stage is a **Kedro pipeline** (`index_build`). Routing, retrieval, and
30	agent search are plain library calls — dynamically branching with a shared budget
31	counter, which makes them unsuitable for a static DAG. A separate Kedro
32	`evaluation` pipeline wraps `evals.evaluate` for reproducible offline benchmarks.
33	
34	`kedro viz` renders both pipeline DAGs when the optional `[viz]` extra is
35	installed.
36	
37	---
38	
39	## Source-described vs replica choices
40	
41	| Feature | NOSIBLE Cybernaut-1 | This replica |
42	|---|---|---|
43	| Index scale | 250 k shards | 8–12 shards (tiny.yaml: 8) |
44	| Build pipeline | 8-stage pipeline | Kedro `index_build` (6 nodes) |
45	| Embedding | Shard-specific LLMs | Hash embedder (offline) or e5-small |
46	| Similarity | Bayesian dense similarity | Exact cosine, float32 |
47	| Search tree | LLM-guided MCTS | Staged beam search with UCT budget allocation (honestly not full MCTS) |
48	| Judge / generator | LLM-based | Heuristic by default (0 LLM calls); `configs/neural.yaml` swaps in a HF cross-encoder judge + Qwen query rewriter on MPS |
49	| Reward max | Unspecified | 1.0 (weights 0.45+0.20+0.20+0.10+0.05·diversity sum to 1.0) |
50	| Retrieval budget | Unspecified | 5+9+4 = 18 calls max |
51	| Stage schedule | Unspecified | Explore 5, Refine 9, Exploit 4 |
52	| Entities | Production NER | Regex fallback (spaCy optional via `[nlp]`) |
53	| Pipelines | Unknown internal | Kedro `index_build` + `evaluation` |
54	
55	---
56	
57	## Environment
58	
59	**Native macOS on Apple silicon is the default.** The devcontainer still builds
60	and is kept for a possible move to AWS, but Docker Desktop's VM is native arm64
61	*Linux*, which is not the same thing as Apple silicon: no Metal, no Neural
62	Engine, and numpy on OpenBLAS rather than Accelerate.
63	
64	```bash
65	make install-mac      # uv sync --extra st --extra mps --extra hf, then verify
66	make accel            # what this machine actually offers
67	```
68	
69	`make accel` resolves rather than assumes:
70	
71	```
72	platform       darwin / arm64  (Apple silicon)
73	numpy BLAS     accelerate
74	numpy SIMD     ASIMDHP,ASIMDDP,ASIMDFHM
75	torch          2.13.0
76	torch backend  mps
77	device         mps
78	fingerprint    mps
79	```
80	
81	`setup_mac.sh` fails loudly on the two things that go wrong silently: numpy
82	linking OpenBLAS instead of Accelerate (so the AMX path is not in play), and
83	torch resolving to `cpu` on Apple silicon (usually an x86 Python under Rosetta).
84	
85	Thread tuning must be exported *before* Python starts — BLAS and OpenMP read
86	their thread counts once, when the shared library loads, so setting them from
87	inside a running process does nothing. `scripts/with-accel.sh` does it and execs:
88	
89	```bash
90	scripts/with-accel.sh uv run cybernaut-mini build ...
91	```
92	
93	On Apple silicon it caps threads at 4. The 8 logical cores are 4 performance +
94	4 efficiency, and a GEMM spread across both waits on the slowest thread.
95	
96	### What acceleration does and does not buy you
97	
98	`embedding.device` (`auto` | `mps` | `cuda` | `cpu`) applies to the
99	`sentence_transformers` provider only; `hash` and `model2vec` never import
100	torch. An unavailable explicit choice degrades to CPU rather than raising, so
101	one config travels between a Mac and a Linux box.
102	
103	Measured on a 16k-document build, the cost is **not** in the parts hardware
104	accelerates:
105	
106	| | |
107	|---|---|
108	| joblib/loky process-pool coordination | ~37s self (`time.sleep`), plus locks and pickling |
109	| Kedro `MemoryDataset` deepcopy | 21.6M calls, ~32s cumulative |
110	| `compute_term_graph` | ~15s — the only real computation in the top five |
111	| embedding (model2vec) | 2.6s |
112	
113	Accelerate and MPS act on the last row. Expect a better place to work, not a
114	dramatically faster build.
115	
116	### Determinism
117	
118	Byte-identical rebuilds are a **per-device** guarantee, not a cross-device one.
119	MPS and CPU do not produce bit-identical vectors — different kernels accumulate
120	in different orders, and no flag makes a GPU reduction match a CPU one bit for
121	bit. `accel.device_fingerprint()` renders the device so an index can record what
122	produced it; comparing two indexes byte-for-byte is only meaningful when their
123	fingerprints agree. The `hash` provider is exempt and stays the offline
124	reproducibility anchor.
125	
126	---
127	
128	## Offline quick start
129	
130	```bash
131	# Install (no GPU, no downloads)
132	uv sync
133	
134	# Build the fixture index — real MIRACL passages + CC-News docs,
135	# hash embedder, 8 shards. data/01_raw/fixtures/ is committed; no download needed.
136	uv run cybernaut-mini build \
137	  --input data/01_raw/fixtures/documents.jsonl \
138	  --index artifacts/fixture \
139	  --config configs/tiny.yaml \
140	  --offline
141	
142	# Inspect shards
143	uv run cybernaut-mini inspect-shards --index artifacts/fixture
144	
145	# Hybrid search
146	uv run cybernaut-mini search \
147	  --index artifacts/fixture \
148	  --question "Is Creole a pidgin of French?" \
149	  --mode hybrid \
150	  --offline
151	
152	# Agent search (three-stage beam search, <=18 retrieval calls, 0 LLM calls)
153	uv run cybernaut-mini search \
154	  --index artifacts/fixture \
155	  --question "What percentage of the Earth's atmosphere is oxygen?" \
156	  --mode agent \
157	  --offline \
158	  --config configs/tiny.yaml \
159	  --trace-out run.json
160	
161	# Evaluate all four modes against the committed MIRACL judgments
162	uv run cybernaut-mini eval \
163	  --index artifacts/fixture \
164	  --judgments data/01_raw/fixtures/judgments.jsonl \
165	  --config configs/tiny.yaml \
166	  --offline
167	```
168	
169	### Kedro equivalents
170	
171	```bash
172	# Build via Kedro (same artifacts as the CLI build above)
173	uv run kedro run --pipeline index_build \
174	  --params "input_path=data/01_raw/fixtures/documents.jsonl,index_path=artifacts/fixture,seed=42,offline=true"
175	
176	# Evaluate via Kedro
177	uv run kedro run --pipeline evaluation \
178	  --params "index_path=artifacts/fixture,judgments_path=data/01_raw/fixtures/judgments.jsonl,offline=true"
179	```
180	
181	---
182	
183	## Artifact formats
184	
185	```
186	artifacts/<index>/
187	  _VALID                     # written last; loaders reject an index without this marker
188	  index_meta.json            # embedding_model, embedding_dim, n_shards, n_documents,
189	                             # seed, artifact_version ("2"; version "1" is rejected)
190	  documents.jsonl            # canonical-JSON, one Document per line (sorted keys)
191	  documents.jsonl.jsonlidx/  # byte-offset sidecar; lets a doc be read without
192	                             # parsing the whole file (rebuilt if missing or stale)
193	  embeddings.npy             # float32 [n_docs x dim], memory-mapped at load
194	  row_map.json               # {doc_id -> row index}; still written, no longer parsed
195	                             # (row lookups go through the documents sidecar)
196	  tokens.jsonl               # {id, tokens} per doc
197	  tokens.jsonl.jsonlidx/     # byte-offset sidecar for tokens.jsonl
198	  shards/
199	    shard_000.json           # ShardManifest: centroid, keywords, entities, term_graph.
200	    ...                      # Shard-id width grows with n_shards, so 1,000+ shards
201	                             # zero-pad to shard_0000.json and still sort lexically.
202	    artifacts/
203	      shard_000.json         # per-shard phrase bloom, zstd dictionary, vocabulary.
204	      ...                    # Stored beside the manifest, not inline in it, and read
205	                             # one shard at a time via LoadedIndex.shard_artifacts().
206	
207	data/01_raw/fixtures/
208	  documents.jsonl      # real MIRACL passages (mir-) + CC-News articles (ccn-)
209	  judgments.jsonl      # 25 MIRACL en-dev queries with graded qrels (grade 0/1)
210	```
211	
212	All JSON artifacts are written through `canonical_dumps` (sorted keys, compact
213	separators, floats rounded to 8 decimal places) so two builds with the same seed
214	and provider are byte-for-byte identical within the same sklearn version.
215	
216	---
217	
218	## Annotated trace example
219	
220	Question: `"transformer scaling laws language model"`
221	Config: `configs/tiny.yaml` (hash embedder, 8 shards, seed 42)
222	
223	```json
224	{
225	  "question": "transformer scaling laws language model",
226	  "seed": 42,
227	  "retrieval_calls": 6,
228	  "llm_calls": 0,
229	  "stop_reason": null,
230	  "final_query": "transformer scaling laws language model graph spaces",
231	  "final_shard_ids": [2, 5, 0],
232	  "selected_path": [0, 3, 5, 6],
233	
234	  "nodes_trimmed": [
235	    {
236	      "node_id": 1, "stage": "explore",
237	      "query": "transformer scaling laws language model",
238	      "shard_ids": [2, 5, 0, 1, 7, 4, 3, 6],
239	      "reward": 0.4726,
240	      "reward_components": {
241	        "relevance": 0.36, "coverage": 1.0,
242	        "dense": 0.3244, "lexical": 0.4666, "redundancy": 0.0192
243	      },
244	      "judge_reason": "heuristic: rel=0.36 cov=1.00 red=0.02 over 5 hits"
245	    },
246	    {
247	      "node_id": 3, "stage": "explore",
248	      "query": "transformer scaling laws language model graph",
249	      "reward": 0.4851,
250	      "judge_reason": "heuristic: rel=0.40 cov=1.00 red=0.02 over 5 hits"
251	    },
252	    {
253	      "node_id": 5, "stage": "refine",
254	      "query": "transformer scaling laws language model graph spaces",
255	      "shard_ids": [2, 5, 0, 1, 3],
256	      "reward": 0.5342,
257	      "judge_reason": "heuristic: rel=0.46 cov=1.00 red=0.02 over 5 hits"
258	    },
259	    {
260	      "node_id": 6, "stage": "exploit",
261	      "query": "transformer scaling laws language model graph spaces",
262	      "shard_ids": [2, 5, 0],
263	      "reward": 0.5281,
264	      "judge_reason": "heuristic: rel=0.46 cov=1.00 red=0.02 over 5 hits"
265	    }
266	  ]
267	}
268	```
269	
270	**Trace annotations:**
271	
272	- **Node 0 (root)**: original question, no retrieval.
273	- **Explore (nodes 1-3)**: heuristic generator emits up to 5 deduplicated
274	  candidate queries. Each executed once (1 retrieval call each). Reward is a
275	  weighted sum of heuristic judge scores plus min-max-normalised dense/BM25
276	  means. Top 3 by mean value survive.
277	- **Refine (nodes 4-5)**: UCT selects which parent to expand next (unvisited
278	  first, then UCT score with `c=1.2`, ties broken by action type then payload).
279	  Node 5 adds "spaces" as a term-graph expansion, raising reward from 0.479 to
280	  0.534.
281	- **Exploit (node 6)**: winner gets 2 children, narrowed to 3 shards, 40
282	  hits/shard. Node 6 is selected as terminal winner (highest mean value across
283	  all nodes).
284	- **Reward formula**: `0.45 x relevance + 0.20 x coverage + 0.20 x dense_norm
285	  + 0.10 x lexical_norm + 0.05 x (1 - redundancy)`. Weights sum to 1.0, so a
286	  perfect, non-redundant result set scores exactly 1.0.
287	- **Budget**: 6 retrieval calls total, well within the 18-call limit (5+9+4).
288	- **UCT**: staged beam search, not full MCTS. The "MCTS" label in the NOSIBLE
289	  post inspired the design, but the implementation is a staged beam with UCT
290	  ordering in the Refine phase only.
291	
292	---
293	
294	## Evaluation results (fixture corpus, offline, seed 42)
295	
296	Run: `uv run cybernaut-mini eval --index artifacts/fixture --judgments data/01_raw/fixtures/judgments.jsonl --config configs/tiny.yaml --offline`
297	
298	```
299	Mode           Recall@5    Recall@10       MRR@10      nDCG@10    Ret calls    LLM calls   Wall (s) (informational)
300	-------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------------
301	lexical          0.5972       0.6944       0.9583       0.7935          1.0          0.0                       0.01
302	dense            0.5833       0.6111       1.0000       0.7902          1.0          0.0                       0.01
303	hybrid           0.6111       0.6528       0.8194       0.7019          1.0          0.0                       0.01
304	agent            0.6528       0.6944       0.8194       0.7140          6.3          0.0                       0.21
305	```
306	
307	**When agent mode underperforms baseline hybrid:** On this small synthetic corpus
308	(63 docs, 12 queries) the agent mode does not consistently beat hybrid. In this
309	run, agent achieves higher Recall@5 and Recall@10 but lower MRR@10 and nDCG@10
310	than the simple lexical baseline. This is expected: the three-stage search is
311	designed to add value when the retrieval space is large and a good initial query
312	is hard to formulate. On 63 documents, a single BM25 or cosine call often
313	retrieves the top result on the first try, and 6.3 extra retrieval calls per
314	query add overhead without proportional quality gain. On a real-scale index
315	(250 k+ shards), routing and refinement would provide substantially more benefit.
316	
317	---
318	
319	## Replica-specific design choices
320	
321	| Decision | Value | Rationale |
322	|---|---|---|
323	| Reward weights | 0.45/0.20/0.20/0.10/0.05 (diversity = 1 − redundancy) | Sum to 1.0; a perfect non-redundant result set scores 1.0 |
324	| Agent judge (opt-in) | `cross-encoder/mmarco-mMiniLMv2-L12-H384-v1` on MPS | Real (question, doc) relevance; multilingual to match CC-News + MIRACL |
325	| Agent generator (opt-in) | `Qwen/Qwen2.5-0.5B-Instruct` on MPS, greedy | Real query rewrites from search state; heuristic fallback on bad output |
326	| Retrieval-call budget | 5+9+4 = 18 | Stage schedule from spec resolution #1 |
327	| Default embedder | `model2vec` (`potion-multilingual-128M`) | Semantic vectors with no torch; shard k-means needs a meaningful space |
328	| Hash embedder dim | 256 (tiny: 256, tests: 64) | `hashlib.blake2b` token+char-trigram buckets, L2-norm |
329	| spaCy | Optional `[nlp]` extra | Regex fallback tested by default; `en_core_web_sm` auto-detected |
330	| Byte-for-byte determinism | Same seed + provider + sklearn version -> identical | `canonical_dumps` + float32 npy |
331	| tiny.yaml shards | 8 | ~7-8 docs/shard for 63-doc corpus |
332	| default.yaml shards | 12 | Default per spec |
333	
334	---
335	
336	## Kedro vs library boundary
337	
338	| Layer | Technology | Reason |
339	|---|---|---|
340	| `index_build` | Kedro pipeline | Pure map-reduce DAG; reproducible, replayable |
341	| `evaluation` | Kedro pipeline | Pure map-reduce DAG; offline benchmarks |
342	| Routing / retrieval | Python library | Per-request; input is a question string, not a dataset |
343	| Agent search | Python library | Shared budget counter, UCT ordering, cannot be a static DAG |
344	
345	Search is not a Kedro pipeline because retrieval branches dynamically at runtime
346	(UCT selects the next node to expand based on prior results), and the budget
347	counter is shared across all three stages in a single request. Kedro's data
348	catalog model assumes a static, pre-known DAG — which the agent's tree search
349	violates. `kedro viz` renders only the `index_build` and `evaluation` pipelines.
350	
351	---
352	
353	## Limitations and ethical-use notes
354	
355	- **Educational only.** Not a production search system. Results on real corpora
356	  depend heavily on embedding quality.
357	- **Three embedding providers, ascending cost.** The default is `model2vec`:
358	  static (lookup-table) embeddings distilled from a real transformer, so they carry
359	  semantic structure without pulling in torch. It is a core dependency, but it
360	  downloads weights (~100 MB) on first use.
361	  - `hash` — feature hashing of tokens and character trigrams. Fast, fully offline,
362	    byte-deterministic, and a first-class provider rather than a test mock. But it
363	    has *no* semantic structure: paraphrases land in unrelated buckets. Selected by
364	    `--offline` and `configs/tiny.yaml`. It is no longer the default because shards
365	    are k-means clusters over document vectors, and clustering only yields coherent
366	    shards if the space carries meaning — with hashing, shard selection looks broken
367	    when the real fault is the embedder.
368	  - `sentence_transformers` — the quality ceiling. Needs `uv sync --extra st` (or
369	    `make install-prod`) and internet on first run; opt in with
370	    `--config configs/default.yaml` (CLI) or `--env prod` (Kedro).
371	- **Small corpus.** The 63-doc synthetic corpus is for testing; metric numbers
372	  above should not be extrapolated to real workloads.
373	- **sklearn version drift.** KMeans output depends on the installed sklearn
374	  version. Byte-identical builds are guaranteed within the same environment only.
375	- **rank-bm25.** Unmaintained but stable for educational use.
376	- **No benchmark claims.** This replica has not been evaluated against any
377	  published NOSIBLE benchmark.
378	- **Unaffiliated.** Not affiliated with, endorsed by, or connected to NOSIBLE
379	  in any way.
380	- **License.** MIT. See `LICENSE`.
381

content.text:
There are really two axes of "two paths" in this repo, and both are deliberate design boundaries. Here's how they fit together.

## Path 1: Build time — Kedro pipelines (static DAGs)

Everything that turns raw documents into a queryable index runs as Kedro pipelines, registered in `src/cybernaut_mini/pipeline_registry.py:17`:

- **`corpus_ingest`** — pulls the two document sources (CC-News + MIRACL) and merges them
- **`judgment_ingest`** — loads MIRACL qrels into `Judgment` records
- **`index_build`** — the 6-node map-reduce DAG: shard (MiniBatchKMeans), embed, write artifacts
- **`evaluation`** — wraps `evals.evaluate` for reproducible offline benchmarks
- **`production`** — chains ingest → judgments → build in one run

These are Kedro pipelines because they're pure, static map-reduce DAGs: inputs and outputs are known up front, so they're reproducible and replayable, and `kedro viz` can render them. This path is configured by **`conf/`** (base/local/prod — Kedro's catalog and parameters).

## Path 2: Query time — plain library calls behind the Typer CLI

Routing, retrieval, and agent search (`routing.py`, `retrieval.py`, `agent/`) are deliberately *not* pipelines — they're library code invoked per request via `cybernaut-mini search`. The reason, stated in the README's "Kedro vs library boundary" section: the three-stage agent search (Explore → Refine → Exploit) branches **dynamically** — UCT picks which node to expand based on results so far, and an 18-call retrieval budget is shared across all stages of a single request. Kedro's data catalog assumes a static, pre-known DAG, which a tree search violates. This path is configured by **`configs/`** (`tiny.yaml`, `default.yaml`, `neural.yaml`).

So the two config directories mirror the two execution paths: `conf/` = Kedro/build, `configs/` = CLI/search.

## The other "two paths" you might have meant: offline fixture vs prod

Cutting across both of the above is a data/model axis:

| | Offline / fixture path | Prod path |
|---|---|---|
| Data | committed `data/01_raw/fixtures/` (63 docs, 25 MIRACL queries) | full CC-News + MIRACL via `corpus_ingest`, 256 shards (`conf/prod`) |
| Embedder | `hash` (blake2b feature hashing, byte-deterministic, zero downloads) | `model2vec` default, `sentence_transformers` as the quality ceiling |
| Judge/generator | heuristic, 0 LLM calls | `configs/neural.yaml` swaps in a HF cross-encoder judge + Qwen query rewriter on MPS |
| Config | `configs/tiny.yaml` + `--offline` | `configs/default.yaml` / `--env prod` |

The offline path exists as a reproducibility anchor — everything runs with no network and byte-identical rebuilds — while the prod path trades that for semantic quality.

If you meant something narrower by "2 paths" (e.g., specifically the CC-News vs MIRACL sources in the ingest DAG, or the CLI-vs-Kedro build equivalence), let me know and I can go deeper on that one.
